implementation: RFC 0017 working tree; tests and documentation are included in the change, no merge claimed
environment: macOS arm64 Darwin 25.6.0; Homebrew LLVM/Clang 23.1.0; CMake Release (-O3 -DNDEBUG), warnings as errors, no sanitizers or LTO for performance measurements

measurement.policy: All six full five-project observations retained. Runs are sequential within each side, with no builds, tests, profiler/checker processes or clang-tidy overlapping corpus measurement. Wall time includes checker startup and the memory wrapper. Project times are medians; total is the median of per-run sums, not the sum of project medians. Peak RSS is the maximum per-checker peak across runs, never the sum. Baseline log.c warmup is retained.
measurement.interpretation: Both targets exceeded. RFC requires investigation and documentation of excess. Largest remaining cost is Lua; see validation report for observed dense numeric-write state and convergence fixes. No claim that remaining time is fully attributed.

tests.clang_tidy: modified/new implementation translation units checked with strict warnings; Core header check included
tests.note: Full Debug and sanitizer suites passed. The shared numeric sidecar fixture was then expanded; all 100 lit tests were rerun in both configurations. No implementation code changed after the corpus binary was built.

diagnostic_comparison: Multiset of project, relative file, line, column, severity, stable ID and exact primary message; before/after counts retain multiplicity. All changed keys included, unchanged records omitted. Diagnostic notes are not in the corpus JSON.

triage_categories.unsupported extent interval projection: Combining a pointer displacement with an independent symbolic byte count exceeds the remaining affine interval projection. The C count can be represented while the combined first/end interval is unresolved.
triage_categories.incompatible or unknown object view at c: Numeric dependencies and changed guards alter the required call footprint. A compatible projection through callback userdata or mutable heap/VM views is unavailable; this is not a confirmed bad-layout call. Exact internal branches were not traced for every site.
triage_categories.call context input path limit reached: Expanded numeric dependencies interact with the existing bounded call-input footprint. A limit is reached at this site; a removed report does not imply that the whole call is verified.
triage_categories.unrepresentable call context input path: The bounded call interface cannot project a required dependency through this stack, heap, callback or selected path. Changes in dependencies can move a coverage boundary without proving the call safe.
triage_categories.unresolved call alias relationship: The required call-input relationships cannot all be represented. cJSON minify_string passes linked cursors into one in-place buffer; Lua has a mutable VM/callback interface. This is incomplete coverage, not an aliasing violation.
triage_categories.unresolved array element selection: Typed arithmetic and bitwise selectors change which sparse cells are representable. Removed selectors in history, hash buckets and VM dispatch can become represented expressions or encounter a different bounded-array limit.
triage_categories.unresolved array element update: A typed computed selector changes whether a selected write is representable. Removing this warning does not establish that its index is in bounds.
triage_categories.array element limit reached: Typed Lua instruction/bitfield selectors become representable, but their possible selected cells exceed the 64-cell budget. This often replaces an opaque selector boundary, not an out-of-bounds finding.
triage_categories.integer expression limit reached: Expanded Lua arithmetic/bitfield expressions exceed the 64-node or depth-12 expression budget. The discarded expression is now explicitly reported as missing coverage.
triage_categories.array range membership is unresolved: For the represented modular copy count, copied and untouched cell alternatives are both retained. Undecided membership alone no longer emits incomplete coverage; this is not a bounds proof.
triage_categories.unsupported memory copy of pointer-conta: The linenoise history suffix copy now retains pointer contents with its typed count. An extent interval projection warning remains at the same operation.
triage_categories.unresolved array range at call: Jansson array_move receives a represented typed count after the insertion/removal guard. Subsequent materialization may still report unsupported array range selection.
triage_categories.unsupported array range selection: Jansson insert writes a selected cell after a saved range move; source-index translation, cell type or the bounded selection cannot fully materialize the range. The exact failed internal branch was not traced.
triage_categories.unchecked history strdup failure: linenoise.c:1583-1584 frees the current history entry and stores unchecked strdup. With two entries, PREV can store null in slot 1 and select valid slot 0; a later NEXT saves slot 0, selects still-null slot 1 and reaches strlen(NULL) at 1598. Source-level path confirmed; no fault-injection reproducer was executed and no claim is made that the analyzer followed that exact two-call path.
triage_categories.successful array table replacement: Jansson value.c:513-530 returns the old table without growing, or calls jsonp_realloc, returns on failure and installs the successful replacement in array->table before the three reported accesses. memory.c:39-60 returns the realloc or allocate/copy/free replacement. These are false positives under the allocator contract. Old-table release state surviving conditional replacement/projection is an inferred cause, not a trace-confirmed one. Unchecked size arithmetic is a separate concern.
triage_categories.nonempty sorted-list tail: In cJSON_Utils.c sort_list, a selected non-null list element initializes result and result_tail together. The else branch dereferences the tail only for a nonempty result, and the post-loop empty-result returns precede the tail writes. These three old null reports were false positives; the exact internal removal cause is inferred to be improved numeric/guard precision.
triage_categories.Lua string buffer success-or-error: str_rep checks its positive count/size branch and obtains p from luaL_buffinitsize. lauxlib.c prepbuffsize returns existing live buffer storage or installs a successful resized buffer; failure raises the Lua error. The old memcpy null report was a false positive. Its removal is consistent with changed numeric guards; the exact internal trace was not isolated.
triage_categories.stdin is not closed by loadfile: lua.c doREPL formerly inherited a double release of stdin. lauxlib.c luaL_loadfilex selects stdin when filename is null and closes lf.f only under if(filename). These branches exclude closing stdin. The removal is consistent with refined typed guards/context effects; the exact internal cause was not traced.
